The delta is a pure insertion and removes nothing. argv git diff --numstat c274df8 HEAD -- crates/foundry-acceptance/, exit 0: 24 added, 0 removed, in the feature file alone. A file with zero deleted lines cannot have weakened an observation held in it. The single hunk opens after line 1365, so every S2 locator keeps its line as well as its bytes: the seven S2 acceptance rows still read at 1202, 1234, 1254, 1275, 1299 (the Scenario Outline with its four credential-count rows), 1326 and 1349, the same lines this record approved at c274df8. The inserted block is six comment lines and one scenario of S3, "While this Foundry opens its secrets key, a start over confirmed from a tab left open changes nothing", tagged @us-iis-07 @error. Its title collides with no other: argv on the file's scenario titles, sorted, uniq -d, exit 0, empty output. It defines no step and changes none: the steps file and the support file are outside the delta, so every binding each S2 scenario calls is byte-identical. Byte identity of the oracle is exact: sha256 f5d5f968888f4f61b38b6ec3afdba2adb8841dbaba9c205c1aa89c4b9bcef0ad for the feature file at HEAD, at d3e277c and in the working tree.

Every S2 observation still runs and still holds under the post-delta bytes, cited from the root-supplied run and not re-executed, because the oracle bytes of that run are the HEAD bytes (same sha256 above). Log /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jeffbailey-Projects-canzan-foundry/ae6f0864-8ca5-43d5-b970-fb78c37ae831/scratchpad/lane-e17-red.log: 30 scenarios (29 passed, 1 failed), 527 steps (526 passed, 1 failed), 0 parsing errors, 0 hook errors. All seven S2 locators are present in that run, at log lines 531, 566, 591, 615, 641/664/687/710 (the outline's four rows), 733 and 758, with no failure marker on any of them; the one failure is the step at feature line 1385, inside the inserted S3 scenario, which is the E17 semantic RED that production commit 0068420 then answered. So the added scenario cannot mask an S2 regression either: it is a separate scenario that fails on its own, and the lane counts rose from 29 to 30 scenarios rather than replacing one. Production changed after that run (0068420 touched secrets_key.rs and secrets_key_rotation.rs only), which is why the run is cited for the executability and content of the S2 observations rather than for GREEN; the repository's own S3 craft record at this commit reads 30 scenarios (30 passed), 532 steps (532 passed), exit 0, a producer-recorded run I did not execute. Implementation GREEN stays a completion obligation of this value.

The only semantic overlap between the inserted scenario and an S2 observation is additive, not substitutive. The inserted scenario reads the 2-credential cost sentence once, while the instance key is still lost, before its own stimulus: the confirmed post sent after the key came back. The S2 Scenario Outline at 1299 remains the sole observation of the cost sentence as a page read, and it alone covers the counts the promise names, 0, 1 (twice, from a saved Slack app and from a workspace connection) and 2, together with the I-28a confirmation field and the pair that proves reading discards nothing. Dropping that outline would lose three of its four counts and both of those further reads, so the inserted read neither replaces it nor makes it redundant. The healthy-key S2 scenario at 1349 likewise keeps its whole observation and its title; the new scenario states a different precondition (a start over confirmed from a tab left open) and a different stimulus (the typed confirmation posted), and asserts the same preservation pair independently. No S2 promise, expectation E11, E12, E14, E15, E16, E17, E18 or E26, loses a falsifier in this delta.
